Study Linking Tumors in Rats to Cellphones Raises a Host of Questions

Highlights I noted from the article:

Even for males, the differences between particular groups of rats and the control group were not statistically significant.

Neither of the groups tested were statistically significant. That means the rates were basically unchanged. So if that's the case, why is this "Study Linking Tumors in Rats" at all? It's the exact opposite - "Study Fails to Link with Tumors in Rats!"

The amounts of radiation that rats were exposed to might be higher than what cellphone users typically experience, though toxicology studies often use higher doses to make sure to detect any effect that might exist.

We always see this mentioned, but I feel it's actually quite important to bring this stuff up. Often when trying to determine toxicity, they'll give massive doses. I mean come on, the term LD50 means "Less than 50% survived this dose." They had mice basically bathed in radiation 24/7 but defined it entirely in wattage. Was it a noise generator? What were the dominant frequencies?

So we can just dismiss this study and go on using our phones? Not totally. As the authors of the report write: “Given the extremely large number of people who use wireless communication devices, even a very small increase in the incidence of disease resulting from exposure to the RFR generated by those devices would have broad implications for public health.”

Not very convincing for me.

“I think this is real,’’ he said, suggesting people used wired earpieces to talk on cellphones. What have other studies found? ... Dr. Carpenter’s view is not the prevailing one. ... The results are reassuring. There is no convincing evidence of any link between cellphone use and cancer or any other disease. Also, the incidence of brain cancer in the United States has remained steady since 1992, despite the stark increase in cellphone use.

So, the guy's study didn't confirm his expectations, and he's trying to make it sound like they do. Good to see the article calls him out on it.

But don’t we know that radiation causes cancer? Ionizing radiation, the powerful type from nuclear weapons, nuclear power plants and X-ray machines, is strong enough to knock electrons off atoms and damage DNA. That can cause cancer. But the radiation from cellphones, called radio-frequency radiation, is nonionizing and not known to damage DNA.

We need to get this information further out there, as I think it's the majority of where this fear of cell phones comes from. "Radiation" is stigmatized and blurred between two definitions: Electromagnetic waves and Nuclear decay radiation."

So what happens now? The findings released Friday are preliminary and part of a larger study, so more data will be coming out, probably next year. The existing report will also be reviewed further by more experts.

As always, stay skeptical and keep looking for more evidence. Article is pretty good, by my standard.
